root_cause.text: The interlaced plain extent classification incorrectly only checked start position alignment but not on-disk physical length alignment, allowing crafted extents with unaligned physical lengths to be treated as interlaced, leading to an out-of-bounds read in z_erofs_transform_plain() due to incorrect data processing assumptions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)` to `!((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)`, explicitly requiring both the physical address and physical length to be block-aligned (bmask = sb->s_blocksize - 1) for interlaced classification.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the condition from `!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)` to `!((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)`, explicitly requiring both the physical address and physical length to be block-aligned (bmask = sb->s_blocksize - 1) for interlaced classification.

candidates.rationale: This condition only checks start position alignment (m_pa) but fails to verify physical length alignment (m_plen). Therefore, extents with unaligned physical lengths can still be classified as interlaced, leading to incorrect data processing assumptions.
